value.hook: Open before probing ~/.pij-rs/pij.sqlite or cleaning temp files during a review.
value.title: Store probes: one process on a read-only copy; delete only your own temp path

sections.name: body
sections.value:
#312 (F258 B1, seats_by_pane), verdict PASS at 6f4c3b9.

What worked: equivalence of a branched query against the generic one, checked on a copy. In ONE python3 process: sqlite3.connect("file:...pij.sqlite?mode=ro", uri=True).backup(copy), apply the migration SQL to the copy, then compare both queries' full rows across every distinct pane × harness × top folders/parents (plus NULL) × live_only. 334,272 combinations, 0 mismatches, in seconds. Also: an injection-shaped bound value returned 0 rows, EXPLAIN showed the index SEARCH, and dropping the index made `INDEXED BY` fail with "no such index". All pane callers map a list error to a refusal, so it is a brake, not a policy.

What went wrong (twice):
1. A shell loop that started sqlite3 for each combination meant thousands of launches. That is a cost incident on this fleet (AGENTS.md § Resource cost). Never loop CLI launches per case; use one in-process connection.
2. Cleanup ran `rm -rf /var/folders/*/*/T/tmp.*`, which may have deleted other seats' in-flight mktemp dirs. pm-001's rule: delete only paths you created and recorded (`T=$(mktemp -d)` ... `rm -rf "$T"`). Never glob a shared temp root: every seat is the same user, the same hazard as kill-by-pattern (D-C34-3). If it happens anyway, disclose it in the verdict and to the requester.
